## Part A: R Pipeline
```{r}
library(tidyverse)

nhanes <- read_csv("examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")

r_summary <- nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), !is.na(Gender)) |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup, Gender) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_bmi = round(mean(BMI), 2),
    sd_bmi = round(sd(BMI), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(IncomeGroup, Gender)
r_summary
```
## Part B: R Function
```{r}
summarise_mean_sd <- function(data, value, group1, group2) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ value }}), !is.na({{ group1 }}), !is.na({{ group2 }})) |>
    group_by({{ group1 }}, {{ group2 }}) |>
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      mean_value = round(mean({{ value }}), 2),
      sd_value = round(sd({{ value }}), 2),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    arrange({{ group1 }}, {{ group2 }})
}

r_function_summary <- summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, BMI, IncomeGroup, Gender)

r_function_summary
```
## Part B Check

```{r}
nrow(r_summary) == nrow(r_function_summary)

identical(
  select(r_summary, IncomeGroup, Gender),
  select(r_function_summary, IncomeGroup, Gender)
)
```
## R Mastery Exercise 1

```{r}
waist_summary <- summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, Waist, IncomeGroup, Gender)

waist_summary
```
The grouping labels stayed the same and the output still had six grouped rows. However, the group counts differed because Waist and BMI have different amounts of missing data.

## R Mastery Exercise 2

```{r}
race_summary <- summarise_mean_sd(nhanes, BMI, Race, Gender)

race_summary
```
This produced 10 grouped rows because there are five Race categories and two Gender categories, giving 5 × 2 combinations.

## Parity Checks
```{r}
nrow(nhanes)
ncol(nhanes)
names(nhanes)

filtered_r <- nhanes |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup), !is.na(Gender))

nrow(filtered_r)
nrow(r_summary)

sum(is.na(nhanes$BMI))
r_summary |>
  select(IncomeGroup, Gender)
```

## Parity Discussion

The R and Python workflows matched on the checks I compared. Both had 105626 rows and 18 columns in the original dataset, 9356 missing BMI values, and 87647 rows after filtering missing BMI, IncomeGroup, and Gender values.

Both workflows also produced the same six IncomeGroup and Gender group labels in the same order. The group counts, mean BMI values, and standard deviations matched after rounding to two decimal places.
